source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Austin campus publishes 19 MW of IT capacity across 242,000 square feet, and that is the only power figure the operator discloses.

The disclosure stops at the campus level. CyrusOne does not say how the 19 MW splits between AUS2 and AUS3, does not publish power density per rack, and does not name a tenant. Any rack count derived from 19 MW depends entirely on a density assumption the operator never states, so the number of AI accelerators this campus could hold is not knowable from the published data.

The certifications describe permitted use, not actual use. PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942 qualify the campus for payment, health, federal, financial, and telecommunications workloads. They say nothing about who occupies the space.

Within Texas, this campus ranks tenth of the 19 facilities that publish a megawatt figure, against a published state total of 475.41 MW, or about 4 percent. Texas has 137 mapped facilities, so the 19 with numbers are a self-selected minority. That share measures disclosure practice, not load on the grid, and this data does not describe the grid at all.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
